# Voice inventory

Generated by `python -B tools/voice_inventory.py`; don't edit by hand, re-run it.
Places are file and function (or constant), without line numbers, so others' edits don't churn it.
Every fixed line a player can read, found by a heuristic scan (see the script), with
who says it (by file, a best guess), where it lives, and **L** when lore's pages
(`docs/lore/`) quote it word for word, usually a line Jeff passed. The guide is
`docs/voice.md`; Jeff's own words in it are never reworded without asking him.

## Only in the party log (16)

Lines whose only delivery is `party_log.add`, the server's own list that her mind reads and no
client is ever sent (748 amended (7)): a player never sees them. Give each a delivery that
reaches the player (a "party" or "speech" message, `_say_plain`, her `_ask_voice`), or a
record by design goes in the tool's LOG_EXEMPT with why. Marked **U** below too.
A line Main builds from another file's text (an offer's result line) isn't caught here.

## Chest titles (4)

A chest's own name is its window's title when `PackPanel.title_name` passes it (a capital, then
only letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens; 787 amended (5)); any other reads "Chest".
**R** marks a title voice has read (the tool's CHEST_TITLES_WORDED); one without is a warning.

|---|---|---|
| R | Offering stone | `levels/barrow/level.json` |
| R | Runner's pack | `levels/barrow/level.json` |
| R | Robbers' chest | `levels/barrow/level.json` |
| R | Robbers' bundle | `levels/barrow/level.json` |

| L | The door of the Hall of Fallen Souls closes behind whoever enters, and opens again for gold returned or for his defeat. | `entries[2].facts[13].text` |
|  | The Encolpion Amulet encases blessed ashes that protect the wearer, and gives its holder another chance to fight. | `entries[2].facts[14].text` |
|  | Pip carries the temple's offering down into the crypt and lays it on the offering stone in the Low Hall. | `entries[2].facts[15].text` |
|  | The crypt is dug beneath the temple in Umbrage. | `entries[2].facts[16].text` |
|  | The temple has its own underground, the crypt, and keeps it wherever the temple stands. | `entries[2].facts[17].text` |
|  | The temple's stair down is watched, so the Mound-breakers broke into the old mound outside town and dug through from it to the crypt. | `entries[2].facts[18].text` |
|  | The Mound-breakers, the grave robbers in the crypt, have been looking for a way to break through to the holy relics, to sell them on the black market. | `entries[2].facts[19].text` |
|  | The Tomb Sledge, a heavy hammer, is carried by the biggest of the grave robbers; the rest cannot lift it, and the broken walls and smashed tombs in the crypt are its work. | `entries[2].facts[20].text` |

|  | Brand the Ox, the biggest of the Mound-breakers, carries the key to their chest. | `entries[2].facts[22].text` |
|  | The spirit of a fallen holy knight of Theus keeps watch in the crypt's First Hall, beside the bier at the foot of the temple stair; his bones lie beneath the temple, held by the draugr. | `entries[2].facts[23].text` |

|  | A traveller on the hills road was caught by raiders; they took his pack but missed a note in his coat. | `entries[21].facts[1].text` |
|  | Before the raiders caught him, the traveller hid his goods under a cairn north of the hills road, east of where he lies. | `entries[21].facts[2].text` |
|  | Some years ago hill folk and Blood Rot raiders fought in the hills, and the broken gear still lies where they fell. | `entries[21].facts[3].text` |
|  | One of the hill folk who fell in that fight was buried where he fell, the barrow being too far, and someone still brings his grave fresh offerings. | `entries[21].facts[4].text` |
|  | His kin left the town for the hills after the fight and keeps a lean-to there, and is often out. | `entries[21].facts[5].text` |
